analysis.title: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD): Strong outlook as datacenter strength translates to 80% growth in 2027 despite PC headwinds - Buy
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on AMD and expects the stock to trade higher after 3Q26 results and 4Q guidance. Investor expectations had been lowered after Intel's weak guidance the prior week.
3Q26 revenue was $13.4bn, versus GS at $13.3bn and the Street at $13.1bn. Non-GAAP EPS (excl. SBC) was $2.09, versus GS at $2.03 and the Street at $1.95.
Datacenter revenue was $8.5bn, up 97% YoY, versus GS at $8.26bn and the Street at $8.24bn. Server CPU revenue hit a record, and initial MI455 GPU shipments to customers began in 3Q.
Management expects OEMs including HPE, Dell, Lenovo and SuperMicro to ramp MI455-based shipments in 4Q.

AMD expects CY27 Datacenter revenue growth of well over 100% YoY and company revenue growth of over 80%. Management expects server CPU revenue to grow 100% YoY in 2027, helped by increased supply availability.
Server CPU revenue is expected to grow 20% QoQ in 4Q after strong demand following the Venice launch. AMD expects the server CPU TAM to grow at a ~50% CAGR through 2030 to $220bn.

4Q26 revenue guidance midpoint is $17.0bn, below GS at $17.6bn and above the Street at $16.3bn. Datacenter is guided up about 50% QoQ, Embedded up double digits QoQ, and Client/Gaming down over 20% QoQ.

4Q26 non-GAAP gross margin guidance is 55%, versus GS at 54.4% and the Street at 55.3%. GS expects gross margin to stay near 55% through 2027 as server CPU tailwinds and fixed-cost absorption offset the GPU ramp mix.
Management expects significant 2027 operating leverage, with OpEx growing at less than half the rate of revenue growth of above 80%.
Implied 4Q26 non-GAAP EPS (excl. SBC) is $2.92, versus the Street at $2.65 and GS at $2.97.
GS raises CY26-28 EPS estimates by an average of 11%, mainly on higher revenue assumptions. CY27E revenue is $101.96bn (from $95.87bn), and CY27E Datacenter revenue is $83.7bn (from $75.5bn).
Client revenue estimates are cut for all three years (CY27E -17.8%), reflecting PC headwinds. Client revenue of $2.95bn in 3Q26 was 5.7% below GS and 4.2% below the Street.
GS lowers its 12-month price target to $675 from $700 on a 30x P/E (from 32x, on lower peer multiples) applied to normalized EPS of $22.50 (from $22.00). The stock closed at $483.90 on 3 Nov 2026.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $675 from $700 as the P/E multiple falls to 30x from 32x on lower peer multiples, partly offset by higher normalized EPS of $22.50. GS sees AMD gaining compute share through CPUs and a wider set of AI accelerator customers.

earnings_insights: AMD 3Q26 reported 11/3: revenue $13,377mn vs GS $13,268mn and Street $13,114mn. YoY growth was 44.7%.

3Q26 non-GAAP EPS (excl. SBC) reported $2.09 vs GS estimate $2.03 and Street estimate $1.95. Gross margin (excl. SBC) was 55.9% vs GS 56.2% and Street 56.1%. Operating margin was 29.3% vs GS 28.7% and Street 28.0%.

3Q26 segments reported: Data Center $8,546mn (GS $8,262mn, Street $8,249mn), Gaming $773mn (GS $756mn, Street $674mn), Embedded $1,109mn (GS $1,124mn, Street $1,094mn), Client $2,949mn (GS $3,126mn, Street $3,077mn).

4Q26 guidance: revenue midpoint $17.0bn (range $16.49-17.51bn) vs GS estimate $17.6bn and Street estimate $16.3bn. Non-GAAP gross margin 55% (GS 54.4%, Street 55.3%), OpEx $3.75bn, OI&E $4mn, non-GAAP tax rate 13%. Implied non-GAAP EPS (excl. SBC) $2.92 vs Street estimate $2.65 and GS estimate $2.97.
GS estimates, new vs old: CY26E EPS (excl. SBC) $8.13 (old $8.05), CY27E $19.20 (old $17.10), CY28E $27.35 (old $25.20). CY27E revenue growth 94.8%, versus management's 'over 80%'.

trade_ideas.description: Buy $AMD, 12-month price target $675 (30x P/E on normalized EPS of $22.50)
trade_ideas.rationale: Datacenter CPU and GPU strength supports over 80% company revenue growth in 2027, with gross margin holding near 55%.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower-than-expected adoption of agentic AI, slower deployment of AMD GPUs related to the Meta deal, share erosion of x86 architecture in enterprise AI, and lack of operating leverage.
